the_signal.headline: AI legal advice failures expose agentic reasoning gaps in high-stakes domains
the_signal.body: Australia's Fair Work Commission just condemned AI-generated legal advice as 'plain wrong'—a public warning that agents operating in regulated domains (legal, financial, healthcare) need explicit verification loops, not just confidence scores. For GTM teams selling into compliance-heavy verticals, this signals a hard requirement: your automation must surface reasoning chains and audit trails, not hide them. This isn't a technical fix—it's a go-to-market requirement that separates defensible automation from liability.

thread_of_day.title: RPA vs. Workflow Automation: Which Actually Lasts?
thread_of_day.takeaway: RPA breaks under scale because it's UI-bound; workflow automation wins on observability, security, and maintainability—pick workflow automation if you're building GTM systems that need to survive handoffs and compliance audits.

whats_moving.context: Amazon Bedrock's multi-agent triage pattern (one router, three specialists) is the live blueprint—GTM orgs are now decomposing monolithic agents into role-based teams that remember customer context across sessions.

whats_moving.topic: Workflow automation vs. RPA positioning sharpening
whats_moving.context: Enterprise buyers are now explicitly comparing these two, and workflow automation is winning on governance and observability—if you're selling GTM tools, this is your positioning wedge against legacy RPA.
Vendor lock-in concerns are now explicit enough that n8n alternatives comparison is a top search—GTM teams are demanding deployment flexibility and multi-cloud parity as table-stakes requirements.

act_on_this: Audit your agent workflows for reasoning transparency: if a customer asks 'why did the bot recommend this action?', can you produce a verifiable chain of reasoning? If not, add structured logging and decision tracing before you hit compliance questions in enterprise deals.
